subtopics.title: The Production Cost Statement in One Sweep

questions.question: Direct materials R480 000 and direct labour R360 000 give a prime cost of:
options: R840 000 — the direct costs added together

questions.question: Total cost of production is R1 140 000 and work-in-progress opened and closed at R30 000. Cost of production of finished goods is:
options: R1 140 000 — the opening and closing balances cancel

questions.question: Salesperson's commission belongs in:
options: Selling and distribution cost — it never enters the production cost statement

questions.question: Carriage on raw materials purchased is treated as:
options: Part of direct material cost — it follows the materials it transported

questions.question: Selling price R135, variable costs per unit R90. The contribution per unit is:
options: R45 — each unit's payment toward fixed costs

questions.question: Fixed costs are R360 000 and contribution is R45 per unit. The break-even point is:
options: 8 000 units — fixed costs divided by contribution per unit

questions.question: Production of 12 000 units against a break-even of 8 000 gives a profit of:
options: R180 000 — four thousand units beyond break-even, each dropping its full R45 contribution

questions.question: To add R90 000 of profit at a R45 contribution, the extra units needed are:
options: 90 000 units, because fixed costs must be recovered again
2 000 units — fixed costs are already covered and stay out of the calculation

subtopics.title: Cash Budgets and the Projected Income Statement

questions.question: Credit sales: July R200 000, August R240 000, September R300 000, collected 30 percent same month, 50 percent next, 18 percent second month. September's collections are:
options: R246 000 — ninety plus one hundred and twenty plus thirty-six thousand

questions.question: Bad debts and depreciation appear in:
options: The projected income statement only — neither ever moves cash in the month recorded
Both documents at the same amounts

questions.question: For a company, provisional tax payments and interim dividends paid belong in:
options: The cash budget, in the month the money moves

questions.question: Actual advertising is R4 000 against a budget of R10 000. The best managerial reading is:
options: A saving to be congratulated without question
An arithmetic error in the budget
Proof the budget was too generous
A query — the underspend may explain weak sales, since advertising drives revenue

subtopics.title: Reconciliations, Age Analysis and the VAT Settlement

questions.question: Our payment of R4 000 made on the 30th does not appear on the supplier's statement. The correction is:
options: Subtract R4 000 on the statement side — a timing difference the supplier has not yet recorded

questions.question: An invoice posted twice in our own ledger at R4 800 is corrected by:
options: Subtracting R4 800 from our ledger — each side fixes only its own errors
Splitting the difference between the two sides

questions.question: Debtors of R240 000 include R48 000 at sixty days and R24 000 at ninety days or more, on thirty-day terms. The judgement is:
options: The book is healthy because most debts are current
Thirty percent of the book is overdue beyond terms — charge interest, suspend the oldest accounts, screen new ones
All debtors should be written off

questions.question: Output R69 000, input R48 000, drawings of stock costing R8 000 excluding VAT, bad debts of R4 600 inclusive written off. Owed to SARS:
options: R21 600 — the subtraction plus R1 200 for drawings minus R600 for the bad debt

questions.question: Flour, oil, filling, gas and the packet cost about R6 per vetkoek. These are variable costs because:
options: They travel with every unit made — ten vetkoek cost sixty, a hundred cost six hundred
They are paid to one supplier

questions.question: The R2 400 for the stall spot and gas bottle is fixed because:
options: It rises with every vetkoek fried
It is owed in full whether the month is busy or empty

questions.question: At R10 selling price and R6 variable cost, the six hundredth vetkoek matters because:
options: Six hundred contributions of R4 exactly cover the R2 400 fixed costs — the break-even unit
It is when the gas runs out

questions.question: If flour spikes and each vetkoek eats R7, break-even moves to:
options: Six hundred still — fixed costs did not change
Eight hundred — the thinner R3 contribution needs more sales to cover the same rent

questions.question: The tin list and the earning list differ because:
options: Cash moves on different dates from the earning it belongs to — account customers pay later
One of the lists must contain errors
Earnings are always bigger than cash

questions.question: A brilliant month on paper can still leave the tin empty when:
options: Account customers pay late while suppliers demand cash now

questions.question: The gas refill lands the same week as the big order's ingredient purchases. Good planning is:
options: Moving the refill earlier or arranging supplier grace in advance — managing the timing, not the luck

questions.question: A number sitting far from its budget is best treated as:
options: A question with a mark attached — find the reason before praising or blaming

subtopics.title: Two Sets of Books and the Taxman's Slice

questions.question: The statement says R5 240, her book says R4 400. The R500 Friday payment missing from the statement is:
options: A timing difference sitting on the statement side until the post catches up

questions.question: The R340 charge for flour arriving only next Tuesday is removed because:
options: Goods are recorded when received — the debt is not hers until the delivery lands

questions.question: A registered vendor selling at R11,50 including VAT holds how much for SARS on each sale?
options: R1,50 — fifteen over one hundred and fifteen of the inclusive price

questions.question: Hiding Friday's cash sales from the VAT return is:
options: Legal if the amounts are small
Only a problem for big companies
Spending money held in trust for SARS — theft from the public purse
